title: Gauss relations for equivariant root lifts in a central extension
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, inverse and identity obeying the group identities; it is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On $S$-schemes use the fppf topology, whose covering families are jointly surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Write $\mathbf G_a(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ with addition and $\mathbf G_m(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$ with multiplication, for every $S$-scheme $T$. A group sheaf means a group-valued functor with unique gluing of compatible sections for these coverings. A central exact sequence means that its first map identifies its source with the kernel of its second map, the second map is locally surjective for this topology, and the kernel commutes with every local section of the middle sheaf. Write $G=\operatorname{SL}_{2,S}$ for the group sheaf of determinant-one $2\times2$ matrices of global functions, and put $x(u)=I_2+uE_{12}$, $y(v)=I_2+vE_{21}$, where $I_2$ is the identity matrix and $E_{ij}$ has entry $1$ at $(i,j)$ and zero elsewhere, and $h(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$. Let $Z$ be a separated commutative $S$-group scheme and $1\to Z\to E\xrightarrow{p}G\to1$ a central exact sequence of group sheaves. Let $D=h(\mathbf G_m)$ and assume $D'=p^{-1}(D)$ is commutative. The conjugation action of $E$ on itself factors through $G$ by centrality. Suppose group-sheaf homomorphisms $x',y':\mathbf G_a\to E$ lift $x,y$ and are equivariant for $D$, with $h(s)\cdot x'(u)=x'(s^2u)$ and $h(s)\cdot y'(v)=y'(s^{-2}v)$. For a local unit $t$, define $g'(t)=y'(-t^{-1})x'(t)y'(-t^{-1})$ and $h'(t)=g'(t)g'(1)^{-1}$. Then $h':\mathbf G_m\to D'$ is a group-sheaf homomorphism lifting $h$, and $h'(s)g'(t)=g'(st)$ for local units $s,t$. For all local sections $u,v$ for which $w=1+uv$ is a unit, the following identities hold, without requiring $u$ or $v$ to be units:
$$x'(u)y'(v)=y'(v/w)h'(w)x'(u/w),\qquad y'(v)x'(u)=x'(u/w)h'(w)^{-1}y'(v/w).$$

source.place: Lemma 4.3.3 and proof, printed pp.128--129, followed by equation (4.3.1) and its removal of the unit condition, printed pp.129--130. Read online on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this lemma.

proof.text: Work on an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and abbreviate $X(u)=x'(u)$, $Y(v)=y'(v)$, $G(t)=g'(t)$ and $H(t)=h'(t)$. Matrix multiplication gives $p(G(t))=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&t\\-t^{-1}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $p(H(t))=\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$. Thus $H(t)\in D'(T)$ and $H(1)=1$. Centrality identifies conjugation by $H(s)$ with the given $h(s)$-action, hence $H(s)X(u)H(s)^{-1}=X(s^2u)$ and $H(s)Y(v)H(s)^{-1}=Y(s^{-2}v)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.3, preliminary definitions and first paragraph of proof, p.128.

proof.text: Substitute these two conjugation identities into the three factors defining $G(t)$ to get $H(s)G(t)H(s)^{-1}=G(s^2t)$. Divide this equality by its case $t=1$ to obtain $H(s)H(t)H(s)^{-1}=H(s^2t)H(s^2)^{-1}$. The left side is $H(t)$ because $D'$ is commutative. Given arbitrary units $a,t$ on $T$, use [lem-sfb-fppf-local-unit-square-root] to pass to an fppf covering on which $a=s^2$ with $s$ a unit. There the equality reads $H(at)=H(t)H(a)=H(a)H(t)$. Equality descends because $E$ is an fppf sheaf. Together with $H(1)=1$ and the projection computed in step 1 this proves that the natural transformation $H:\mathbf G_m\to D'$ is a homomorphism lifting $h$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.3, proof, p.128; the passage from squares to arbitrary units is made explicit using Stacks Tag 040N.

proof.text:
Since $G(t)=H(t)G(1)$, multiplicativity gives $H(s)G(t)=G(st)$. Expand both sides and move $H(s)$ across the first $Y$-factor by step 1. Cancel the last $Y(-1/t)$ on the right and multiply on the left by $Y(1/(st))$. Additivity of $Y$ yields
$$Y((s-1)/(s^2t))H(s)X(t)=X(st)Y((s-1)/(st)).$$
For $u$ and $w=1+uv$ units, put $s=w$ and $t=u/w$; then $st=u$, $(s-1)/(st)=v$, and $(s-1)/(s^2t)=v/w$. Thus $X(u)Y(v)=Y(v/w)H(w)X(u/w)$ whenever $u,w$ are units.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.3, last sentence, and equation (4.3.1), p.129; cancellation and substitution written out.

proof.text:
Now suppose only that $w=1+uv$ is a unit. By [lem-sfb-fppf-local-two-unit-decomposition], fppf-locally write $u=a+b$ with $a,b,q=1+bv$ units. Apply step 3 first to $(b,v)$ and then to $(a,v/q)$; their Gauss parameters are respectively $q$ and $1+av/q=w/q$, both units. The result is
$$X(u)Y(v)=Y(v/w)H(w/q)X(aq/w)H(q)X(b/q).$$
The conjugation formula of step 1 gives $X(aq/w)H(q)=H(q)X(a/(qw))$. Multiplicativity of $H$ and additivity of $X$ therefore reduce the right side to $Y(v/w)H(w)X(u/w)$, since $a/(qw)+b/q=(a+bw)/(qw)=u/w$ using $u=a+b$ and $w=1+uv$. This is an equality in $E$ on a covering, so the sheaf axiom gives it on $T$.

source.place: After equation (4.3.1), pp.129--130; local decomposition and two successive applications of the unit case.

proof.text:
Apply step 4 to $(-u,-v)$, whose parameter is again $w=1+uv$. Taking inverses and using that $X,Y$ are homomorphisms from the additive group gives
$$Y(v)X(u)=X(u/w)H(w)^{-1}Y(v/w).$$
All constructions and equalities commute with restriction to $S$-schemes, so these are the required identities of group sheaves, with no unit condition on $u$ or $v$.

source.place: The inverse relation immediately after the simplification of (4.3.1), p.130.
